record.original_question: Can one prove the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) for solutions of the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations without assuming them a priori? Establishing those unconditional regularity estimates would imply global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data.

evidence.quote: Observing the conditional regularity results of Theorems 3.2 and 3.1, the obvious question is whether the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3) can possibly be proved.

If we somehow established the bounds for the hydrodynamic quantities in (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3), we would conclude that the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations have global smooth solutions, for any initial data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff, and the spatially inhomogeneous Landau equation, for a nonnegative density f(t,x,v) on [0,T)×Ω×ℝ³ (with Ω = 𝕋³ or ℝ³). Associated to f are the hydrodynamic quantities

  • mass density M(t,x) = ∫_{ℝ³} f(t,x,v) dv,
  • energy density E(t,x) = ∫_{ℝ³} |v|² f(t,x,v) dv,
  • entropy density H(t,x) = ∫_{ℝ³} f(t,x,v) log f(t,x,v) dv,
  
together with the requirement that the mass density stays bounded away from vacuum.

Conditional regularity theorems for these equations state that, if there exist constants 0 < m₀ ≤ M(t,x), and M(t,x) ≤ M₁, E(t,x) ≤ E₁, H(t,x) ≤ H₁ uniformly on [0,T)×Ω (these are the bounds referred to as (3.1)–(3.3)), then the solution f is C^∞ and remains smooth up to time T.

Problem. Prove these hydrodynamic bounds unconditionally: show that for any sufficiently regular nonnegative initial datum f₀ with finite mass, energy, and entropy (and mass bounded below by a positive constant), the corresponding solution of the inhomogeneous Landau equation (and, separately, of the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation) satisfies uniform upper bounds on its mass, energy, and entropy densities and a uniform positive lower bound on its mass density on any time interval of existence. Consequently, derive the existence of global-in-time smooth solutions for arbitrary such initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (Imbert–Silvestre and subsequent works through 2024–2025) establishes conditional regularity for the inhomogeneous Boltzmann and Landau equations assuming pointwise bounds on the hydrodynamic fields (mass, energy, entropy, and mass bounded away from vacuum), and proves smoothing and L^∞ estimates conditional on these bounds. Unconditional proofs of these macroscopic bounds in the inhomogeneous setting—and hence global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data—remain open; only the homogeneous Landau–Coulomb case has recently seen unconditional global smoothness results.

status_evidence.title: Regularity for the Boltzmann Equation Conditional to Pressure and Moment Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions enjoy uniform L^∞ bounds and C^∞ estimates conditional to macroscopic bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Regularity for inhomogeneous Boltzmann is established only conditionally on macroscopic/hydrodynamic bounds.

status_evidence.title: Regularity for the Boltzmann equation conditional to macroscopic bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Conditional to bounds on mass, energy and entropy densities, solutions are smooth.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art for inhomogeneous Boltzmann/Landau is conditional regularity.

status_evidence.title: Global Smooth Solutions to the Landau–Coulomb Equation in L^{3/2}
status_evidence.snippet: Global-in-time smooth solutions for the homogeneous Landau–Coulomb equation.
status_evidence.claim: Unconditional global smoothness has been obtained in the homogeneous Landau case but not the inhomogeneous one.
